title: Spaced Repetition and AI Conversation: Learn 1,000 Words a Month (July 2026)
summary: July 2026 guide to learning 1,000 words a month with spaced repetition. Covers FSRS, Anki settings, sentence cards, and AI conversation to build
body_text: Thirty-three new cards a day, 90% retention, FSRS doing the math in the background. The spaced repetition side of vocabulary learning is well-documented and genuinely effective. What's less talked about is what happens after the reviews: you've kept 1,000 words alive in your head, but pulling them out during an actual conversation is a separate skill that flashcards alone don't train. This post covers the full loop, from building your daily review schedule to closing the gap between recognition and real use. TLDR: Spaced repetition spaces reviews at widening intervals timed to your forgetting rate; a 2022 meta-analysis by Kim and Webb across 48 experiments found medium-to-large effects on second language retention, with longer intervals producing the strongest gains. Hitting 1,000 words a month means 33 new cards per day, but the real load comes from the review queue: budget 45 to 60 minutes daily and expect 250 to 300 total cards per session by week two. Sentence cards outperform isolated word cards because they carry article gender, case endings, and word order for free, so you rehearse grammar every time you rehearse the word. Drilling 5,000 cards to 90% retention won't prepare you for a real conversation; Swain's Output Hypothesis (1985) argues that producing language under pressure is what moves words from recognition into actual use. ISSEN builds SRS flashcards from your own voice conversations, so the review card surfaces the sentence you used the word in, not a wordlist someone else made. What spaced repetition is Spaced repetition is a review schedule that spaces encounters with a piece of information at widening intervals, timed just before you would forget it. Each successful recall stretches the next interval. Each miss shortens it. A word you saw once becomes a word you own. The mechanic sits on Hermann Ebbinghaus's 1885 forgetting curve, which showed memory decays sharply after initial learning and flattens with each successful review. Sebastian Leitner turned that into a practical system in the 1970s using physical flashcard boxes: cards you got right moved to slower-review boxes; missed cards dropped back to daily practice. Modern AI language learning has since built on these foundations in ways Leitner couldn't have anticipated. For vocabulary, the bottleneck is not exposure. The real constraint is retention under decay. The science of the forgetting curve Ebbinghaus's original curve put numbers on something every learner has felt: Murre and Dros's 2015 replication confirmed that around 60 to 70% of new material slips away within 24 hours if nothing pulls it back. The decay is steep at first, then flattens. Each timed review before the trace fades resets the slope, and the interval you can safely wait grows longer. The empirical version is a 2022 meta-analysis by Kim and Webb covering 48 experiments and 3,411 participants, which found medium-to-large effects on second language learning from spaced practice, with longer intervals producing the strongest gains on delayed retention tests. Same-day cramming quietly evaporates by the following week. The broader picture of effective language learning techniques shows spaced practice as one pillar among several. How SRS algorithms schedule your reviews Under the hood, every spaced repetition app runs the same math: how long can we push the next review without letting the card slip? The classic answer is SM-2, published by Piotr Wozniak in 1987. It multiplies the current interval by an ease factor that shrinks when you miss a card. Simple, but the same schedule for every learner. Anki's current default is FSRS, the Free Spaced Repetition Scheduler. It tracks three variables per card and fits a personalized memory model from your own review history: Difficulty: how hard the card is for you in particular Stability: how long the memory lasts before decay Retrievability: the predicted probability you can recall it right now FSRS schedules the next review when retrievability drops to a target you set (90% is the common default), so intervals stretch or contract based on your actual forgetting rate. As of February 2024, FSRS is supported natively across all Anki clients : desktop, AnkiWeb, AnkiMobile on iOS, and AnkiDroid. Anki for language learning: free, cross-platform, and highly configurable Anki is the tool most committed learners land on, and it stays free where it matters. The desktop app runs on Windows, Mac, and Linux; AnkiWeb syncs decks across devices; AnkiDroid is free on the Play Store. The exception is iOS: AnkiMobile is $24.99 USD, which funds the wider ecosystem. Setting Default for 1,000/month Why New cards/day 33 One month of intake to hit target Reviews/day 200 to 300 Absorbs the tail from prior weeks Scheduler FSRS Personalizes intervals to your recall Desired retention 0.9 Balances workload and accuracy Learning steps 1m 10m Quick early reinforcement After 400 to 1,000 reviews of history, run Tools > FSRS > Optimize to fit parameters to your own forgetting rate. Recheck every couple of months. Why sentence cards outperform isolated word cards A naked card pairs a foreign word with its English gloss and nothing else. You learn that "Schlussel" means "key," then in a real sentence you hesitate over der, die, or das, and whether you need Schlussel, Schlussels, or Schlusseln. A sentence card carries that information for free. The word arrives inside its article, case ending, and word order, so you rehearse the grammar every time you rehearse the word. For German, Russian, or Japanese, that packaging is the difference between recognition and production. Paul Nation's work at Victoria University of Wellington argues deliberate vocabulary learning from word cards is efficient but incomplete. Cards build the foundation. Meaning-focused input and output convert it into words you can pull out mid-conversation. How to build a spaced repetition schedule for 1,000 words a month The math is simple. 1,000 words divided by 30 days is 33 new cards per day. The trap is the review queue: at 90% retention, each new card generates 8 to 10 reviews before intervals stretch past 30 days. A realistic week two load, once the pipeline is full: Day New Reviews Total Mon 33 220 253 Wed 33 260 293 Fri 33 270 303 Sun 33 260 293 Budget 45 to 60 minutes a day. If the queue climbs past 350, pause new cards for two or three days and let reviews drain. Do not drop retention below 0.85 to catch up; you will spend the recovered time relearning leeches. To project your load before committing, plug your new-card rate into Anki's built-in FSRS simulator (Tools > FSRS > Simulate) or a spreadsheet tracking date, new cards, and rolling reviews at your target retention. Active recall vs. passive review Retrieval is the whole engine. Cover the answer, force the word out of your head, and only then flip the card. Re-reading the front and back until it feels familiar gives you a warm sense of recognition that collapses under a delayed test. The Again, Hard, Good, Easy buttons only work if you rate accurately. Hard means you recalled it slowly under strain. Again means you missed it. Pressing Hard on a blank teaches the algorithm the wrong stability curve, and your intervals drift out of sync with your actual forgetting rate. The leech pile grows from there. Why SRS alone won't make you fluent SRS is a retention tool. It keeps a word alive in your head, and that is the whole promise. Recognition and fluent spoken recall run on different circuits, and the flashcard trains only the first one. Solo language speaking practice builds the second circuit separately. You can drill 5,000 cards to 90% retention and still freeze when a cashier asks a follow-up, because pulling a word under real-time pressure is a separate skill built separately, and fear of speaking a foreign language compounds that gap. Grammar has the same problem. Recognizing that a subjunctive is correct on a card does not teach your mouth to reach for it mid-sentence. Case endings, particles, article gender: these become automatic through production reps, not repeated recognition. Cards give you the raw material. Talking converts it, which is why your language routine needs speaking practice built in from the start, not added as an afterthought. How AI conversation practice completes the SRS cycle Merrill Swain's Output Hypothesis argues that producing language under conversational pressure forces you to notice the gap between what you meant to say and what came out. Reading a card labels a word as familiar; reaching for it in a sentence, missing the ending, and hearing yourself correct it: that process moves the word from recognition into production. The historical block has been access. A conversation partner willing to sit through your broken B1 attempts at 6am does not exist for most learners. AI speaking practice removes the scheduling and the flinch of stumbling in front of another human. If Anki keeps your 1,000 words alive, daily conversation forces them into your mouth, and that is exactly what AI language tutoring for speaking fluency is built to deliver. ISSEN: Conversation-Anchored SRS in a Single Session Where a standalone Anki deck starts from a wordlist someone else made, ISSEN's flashcards get built from your own voice conversations, a design that separates the best AI language tutors for conversation practice from simple chat tools. When a word surfaces mid-session, the review card carries the sentence you used it in, the topic, and the situational context. Retention and production close in one workflow. Our CEO Mariano used contextual SRS to learn 2,200 Kanji in 90 days and 2,000 Japanese words in 80 days, under two hours of study per day (per Mariano's personal account). The AI voice tutor drives the exchange and adjusts vocabulary and pace to your level in real time No push-to-talk, so lock-screen sessions on a walk or commute count as real reps Available on iOS, Android, and web with a 10-minute free trial. You can also compare it against the best language learning apps for speaking to find the right fit. Final thoughts on spaced repetition as a language learning system Spaced repetition gives your vocabulary somewhere to live between conversations. The algorithm handles the scheduling; your job is accurate ratings, consistent reviews, and enough speaking practice to make the words feel automatic. Think of Yuna, a Korean nurse who moved to Canada last year aiming to pass her RN licensing interview within three months, and drilled 1,200 medical and workplace terms to 90% retention in Anki, only to freeze in her first staff meeting when a doctor asked a follow-up she hadn't rehearsed. The vocabulary was there; the output circuit wasn't. What changes that is daily conversational pressure: sentences under real-time conditions, corrections in context, and review cards tied to what you actually said. That is the direction the field is moving, and the tools for it are already available. When your deck is ready for a real test, try ISSEN free for 10 minutes and see how many of those words you can actually pull out in real time. FAQ What's the difference between Anki's FSRS algorithm and the older SM-2 for language learning? FSRS tracks three variables per card (difficulty, stability, and retrievability) and builds a personalized memory model from your own review history, so intervals stretch or contract based on how you forget, not a generic curve. SM-2 applies the same ease-factor formula to every learner regardless of individual recall patterns. For a spaced repetition schedule targeting 1,000 words a month, FSRS produces meaningfully better retention per review minute once you have 400 to 1,000 reviews logged and run the optimizer. Can I build a spaced repetition schedule for 1,000 words a month without burning out on reviews? Yes, but the math requires planning before you start. At 90% desired retention, 33 new cards per day generates 200 to 270 reviews per day by week two, so budget 45 to 60 minutes daily and use Anki's built-in FSRS simulator to project your queue before committing. If reviews climb past 350, pause new cards for two or three days; dropping your retention target below 0.85 to catch up costs more time relearning lapsed cards than it saves. How do I use Anki spaced repetition settings for sentence cards instead of isolated word cards? Set your learning steps to 1 minute then 10 minutes, keep desired retention at 0.90, and cap new cards at 33 per day to hit the 1,000-word monthly target. The deeper change is card format: build sentence cards that carry the word inside its article, case ending, and word order so every review rehearses grammar alongside vocabulary. This matters especially for German, Russian, or Japanese, where a word divorced from its morphology is only half the information you need. Why does drilling a spaced repetition vocabulary app to 90% retention still leave you freezing mid-conversation? Recognition and real-time spoken recall are separate skills trained by different kinds of practice. A spaced repetition app trains you to identify a word when it appears on a screen; pulling that same word out of memory while a native speaker is waiting for your answer runs on a different cognitive circuit built through output reps under conversational pressure. Merrill Swain's Output Hypothesis describes this precisely: producing language forces you to notice the gap between what you meant to say and what came out, and that noticing is what moves a word from passive recognition into active use. Vocabulary apps supply the raw material; conversation converts it. Anki spaced repetition vs ISSEN for vocabulary retention: which should I use? Use both, for different jobs. Anki's spaced repetition schedule keeps words alive between conversations through timed retrieval practice, which the 2022 Kim and Webb meta-analysis across 48 experiments confirmed produces medium-to-large effects on delayed retention. ISSEN's AI voice tutor then forces those same words into real-time spoken production, and generates flashcards anchored to the sentences you actually used during the session, so the review card carries the original conversational context and not an isolated gloss. The two tools close different gaps in the same cycle: Anki handles retention under decay; spoken conversation practice handles the transfer from recognition to fluency.

body_text: Vintage fashion continues to be one of the most profitable categories in online resale, but not every label performs equally. The best vintage brands to resell include Levi's, Ralph Lauren, Harley-Davidson, Gunne Sax, Diane von Furstenberg, and many iconic designer labels. These brands consistently attract collectors and fashion enthusiasts because of their quality, history, craftsmanship, and limited supply. As buyers move away from fast fashion and mass-produced " vintage-inspired " clothing, authentic vintage continues to increase in demand across marketplaces like eBay, Etsy, Depop, Poshmark, Grailed, and Vestiaire Collective. Learning which brands buyers actively search for gives resellers a significant advantage when sourcing inventory. Main Takeaways Brands: The best vintage brands to resell include Levi's, Ralph Lauren, Harley-Davidson, Gunne Sax, Guess, Disney, and more. Value: Brand recognition can increase visibility and resale value, but condition, rarity, era, and style are equally important when pricing vintage inventory. Definition: Authentic vintage clothing must be at least 20 years old, while garments that are 100 years old or older are considered antiques. Identification: Learning to identify vintage tags, construction techniques, fabrics, and union labels will help you source more profitable inventory. Listings: Detailed measurements, accurate dating, quality photography, and strong SEO listings help vintage items sell faster and reduce returns. Marketplaces: Selling across multiple marketplaces like eBay, Etsy, Depop, Poshmark, Grailed, and Vinted can increase exposure and improve sell-through rates. What Qualifies as Vintage Clothing? An item is considered vintage once it is at least 20 years old . Clothing that reaches 100 years old is generally considered antique. Understanding this distinction helps sellers categorize inventory accurately, build buyer confidence, and comply with marketplace guidelines. It also prevents modern " vintage-inspired " pieces from being mistakenly marketed as authentic vintage. 🧠 Did you know that there is a huge global market for American Vintage made in the U.S.A.? Why Vintage Clothing Is Trending and Profitable Vintage remains one of the strongest resale categories because every authentic piece has a limited supply. Once a garment is gone, no factories are producing identical replacements. Buyers are increasingly searching for better construction, natural fabrics, unique styles, sustainable fashion, and one-of-a-kind pieces. How to Identify True Vintage Clothing Finding the great vintage brands to resell is only part of the equation . Successful vintage resellers also learn how to recognize authentic vintage garments, especially when the label is missing, unfamiliar, or no longer in business. Fortunately, vintage clothing often reveals its age through construction techniques, materials, labels, and manufacturing details. The more of these characteristics you recognize, the easier it becomes to identify profitable pieces while sourcing. Look for these common indicators: Single stitch construction on t-shirts (rather than the double-stitch used today) Selvedge denim and redline selvedge Paper garment tags Sheer care labels commonly found in dresses intended to be worn with slips Hand-finished hems and seams Metal zippers instead of plastic Union labels, including ILGWU tags Made in USA, Made in UK, or Made in France labels Natural fiber content such as wool, linen, silk, and cotton None of these features alone guarantees that a garment is vintage, but several appearing together can provide strong evidence of its age. Learn to Recognize Union Labels Union labels are one of the most useful dating tools available to vintage resellers. Photo Source: ILGWU label guide by MillenialMouse . Don't Ignore Lesser-Known Brands Many new vintage resellers focus exclusively on recognizable names like Levi's or Ralph Lauren. While those brands are excellent finds, countless lesser-known labels can also sell exceptionally well. Brands such as Jonathan Logan, Carole Little, Albert Nipon, Leslie Fay, Lilli Ann, Koret of California, Pendleton 49er, Lady Manhattan, and White Stag regularly attract vintage buyers despite being less familiar to the average shopper. Instead of judging an item solely by the brand name, evaluate the garment as a whole . Era, quality, style, rarity, and condition often matter just as much as the label itself. Dating Vintage Clothing with AI Artificial intelligence has become one of the most useful research tools available to vintage resellers. While it should never replace your own knowledge, AI can significantly reduce the time required to identify unfamiliar brands and estimate the age of a garment. 💡 Tip: When in doubt, use Google or AI to help determine the age of clothing based on features like stitchwork and labels. Here, I provided ChatGPT with photos of the item and its tag and learned a lot about the brand and the piece's age. When researching a vintage piece, upload clear photos of the following: Front of the garment Back of the garment Brand label Care label Union label, if present Fabric content tag Zippers, buttons, or hardware Distinctive construction details AI can often help identify the approximate decade of production, label variations over time, similar sold examples, and possible keywords. Always verify important information before publishing a listing, particularly for high-value designer pieces. AI is an excellent research assistant, but authentication should still rely on trusted references and your own inspection. Where to Source Vintage Brands The best vintage brands to resell rarely come from a single source . Successful resellers cast a wide net and consistently visit locations where overlooked vintage inventory still appears. The great thing about vintage is that most thrift stores have lots, and most do not charge as much as they do for trendy, modern name brands. Some of the best places to source vintage clothing include: Thrift stores Church rummage sales Estate sales Yard sales Flea markets Storage auctions Consignment stores Facebook Marketplace Community buy-and-sell groups The resale marketplaces themselves. Many experienced vintage sellers develop relationships with estate sale companies, auctioneers, and antique dealers who notify them when vintage clothing collections become available. The most profitable inventory often comes from buying entire collections rather than individual pieces. How to Photograph Vintage Clothing for Online Sales While many sellers photograph on a clear hanger or laid flat, vintage clothing rarely looks its best on a hanger . Because vintage silhouettes, textures, and construction differ significantly from modern garments, modeling or showcasing on a dress form are the most effective ways to showcase fit and style. “ When you buy a piece of vintage clothing, you’re not just buying fabric and thread. You’re buying a piece of someone’s past .” -Isabel Wolff. Image Source: FourLimes on Depop Some resellers style pieces true to the era, while others pair vintage with modern elements for a contemporary look. Both approaches can be successful when the garment’s shape, texture, and details are clearly visible. 💡 Tip: If a picture is worth a thousand words, a video is worth a million. Use listing videos to show off your modeled vintage pieces. Vintage Sizing and Measurement Best Practices Many vintage pieces do not have size tags. Even when they do, vintage sizing differs significantly from modern sizing standards. For this reason, you want to include both the " tagged vintage size " (for accuracy) and the " best modern fit size " (for practicality). For SEO purposes, many vintage sellers select a modern size equivalent as the size when listing. If you have a blouse tagged as a size large, but it fits more like a modern small, listing it as large wouldn't make much sense, as the listing would only be shown to buyers who are size large. Be sure to always include detailed measurements , including chest/bust, shoulders, sleeves, waist, hips, inseam, leg opening, and length. Clear measurements reduce returns and build buyer confidence, especially for higher-value vintage items. For example, this 1980s blouse is tagged size 14P, but would not fit someone who wears a modern 14P. So, I listed it as a large, explaining that large is the best modern equivalent. I included several measurements so buyers can shop with confidence despite the discrepancy in sizing. Vintage Sourcing Guide by Decade While selling popular brands helps increase sales, it's not only about the brand. Many vintage shoppers don't even know or care about the brand: they care about the look and the style. Here is a guide to identify the best styles of each decade. Y2K Fashion and Early 2000s Vintage The early 2000s brought bold, playful fashion inspired by pop culture icons. Y2K fashion is highly sought after by millennials and Gen Z buyers. Paris Hilton, Britney Spears, and Bratz Dolls were fashion icons at this time. High-performing pieces include baby tees, baguette bags, pleated mini and micro skirts, plaid skirts, velour tracksuits, lace camisoles, rhinestone details, and pastel colors. The best vintage brands to sell from the early 2000s include Juicy Couture, Lisa Frank, Ed Hardy, early Alexander McQueen, and playful pop-culture labels. 1990s Vintage Fashion Trends The 1990s were defined by grunge, hip-hop, and minimalist fashion. Popular styles include leather jackets, mom jeans, overalls, cardigans, bucket hats, and bold and bohemian prints like leopard and acid wash. Princess Diana, Kate Moss, and Phoebe Buffay (Lisa Kudrow) were fashion icons of the 90s. The best vintage brands from the 1990s include Levi's, Guess, Gap, Nike, Espirit, Osh Kosh B'Gosh, Calvin Klein, Tommy Hilfiger, Prada, Versace, Comme des Garçons, and COOGI. Vintage band t-shirts from this era can carry extremely high resale value and should always be researched individually. 1980s Vintage Fashion The 1980s were bold and expressive, influenced by music and pop culture icons. Common styles include spandex, track jackets, parachute pants, leg warmers, shoulder pads, and neon colors. Madonna and Cyndi Lauper were top fashion icons in the 80s. The best vintage brands from the 1980s include Harley-Davidson, Levi’s, Ralph Lauren, Victor Costa, Calvin Klein, Guess, Members Only, Reebok, Nike, and Jordache. 1970s Vintage Fashion Image Source: Four Limes Shop, LLC . The 1970s embraced disco, boho, and folk influences. Popular items include smocked dresses, crochet designs, denim dresses, platform shoes, scarves, satin slips, and coordinated sets. 1970s fashion icons included Diana Ross, Cher, and Farrah Fawcett. The best vintage brands from the 1970s include Levi's, Wrangler, Gunne Sax, Diane von Furstenberg, Halston, Lee, Ossie Clark, Missoni, Pendleton, Nike, Dittos, Landlubbers, and Whiting and Davis. 💡Tip: Vintage lingerie from the 70s often carries strong resale value. 1960s Vintage Fashion The 1960s brought revolutionary fashion alongside sweeping political and cultural change, marked by youth-driven style and futuristic experimentation. Defining looks include mini skirts, shift dresses, A-line silhouettes, pillbox hats, go-go boots, mod tailoring, fringe, sequins, vinyl and PVC fabrics, bold geometric prints, color-blocking, and graphic black-and-white patterns. Influential female fashion icons of the decade include Twiggy , Jacqueline Kennedy , and Brigitte Bardot , whose mod, minimalist, and bombshell aesthetics continue to influence vintage demand. The best vintage brands from the 1960s to sell include Pierre Cardin , Emilio Pucci , Mary Quant , Yves Saint Laurent , André Courrèges , Paco Rabanne , Rudi Gernreich , Bonnie Cashin , Givenchy , and Oleg Cassini . 1950s Vintage Fashion The 1950s emphasized polished femininity, structured silhouettes, and pin-up glamour, heavily influenced by post-war optimism and Hollywood style. Defining looks include full circle skirts, poodle skirts, fitted pencil skirts, wiggle dresses, bustier and sweetheart neckline tops, capri pants, cardigans, gingham and polka-dot prints, cat-eye sunglasses, saddle shoes, and cropped leather jackets. 60s fashion icons included Marilyn Monroe , Audrey Hepburn , Elizabeth Taylor , and Grace Kelly. The best vintage brands to sell from the 1950s include Christian Dior, Givenchy, Balenciaga, Lilli Ann, Pendleton, Lanz Originals, Circle T, Lee, Levi’s, and Schott. 💡 Tip : Metal side and back zippers, especially Talon or Conmar, are common indicators of authentic early vintage garments from the 1950s and often increase collector interest. 1940s Vintage Fashion The 1940s were defined by wartime practicality and resourcefulness, with fashion shaped by fabric rationing and utility regulations. Signature styles include shirtwaist dresses, tea dresses, A-line skirts, knee-length hemlines, padded and structured shoulders, tailored suits, utility pockets, and muted or neutral color palettes. Female fashion icons of the 40s include Katharine Hepburn , Rita Hayworth , and Lauren Bacall. The best 1940s vintage brands to sell include Lilli Ann , Adrian , Claire McCardell , Bonnie Cashin , Gabardine , and Junior Vogue . 1930s Vintage Fashion The 1930s emphasized elegance, Old Hollywood glamour, and fluid movement, with fashion shifting toward longer hemlines and body-skimming silhouettes. Defining styles include bias-cut gowns, draped evening dresses, satin and silk fabrics, velvet, softly tailored suits, flutter sleeves, and romantic details influenced by Hollywood film stars. Influential 30s fashion icons include Jean Harlow , Marlene Dietrich , and Greta Garbo. The best vintage brands from the 1930s to sell include Vionnet , Elsa Schiaparelli , Lucien Lelong , Mainbocher , Edward Molyneux , and Jean Patou . 1920s Vintage Fashion The roaring 1920s or the "jazz era" marked a dramatic break from traditional fashion, introducing youthful, modern silhouettes driven by social change and liberation. Signature styles include flapper dresses, dropped waists, straight chemise shapes, cloche hats, beaded and sequined embellishments, fringe, Art Deco motifs, sheer overlays, and the rise of the little black dress. Influential female fashion icons of the decade include Louise Brooks , Josephine Baker , and Clara Bow. The best vintage brands from the 1920s include Chanel , Jeanne Lanvin , Callot Soeurs , Poiret , Worth , and Lucile . The Best Vintage Brands and Styles Finding the best vintage brands to resell is only the beginning. The most successful vintage sellers combine brand knowledge with an understanding of garment construction, dating techniques, accurate pricing, and strong listing practices. As you gain experience, you'll begin recognizing valuable pieces long before other shoppers do. Keep researching unfamiliar labels, study vintage tags and fabrics, and continue refining your sourcing strategy . Over time, those skills will help you uncover hidden gems and build a vintage inventory that stands out across today's most popular resale marketplaces Do you have any tips and tricks for finding and authenticating vintage clothes? Share with us below! 👇🏽 Best Vintage Brands FAQ What is considered vintage clothing? Clothing is generally considered vintage once it is at least 20 years old. Items that are 100 years old or older are typically classified as antiques. Authentic vintage should not be confused with modern "vintage-inspired" clothing Which vintage brands sell for the most money? Brands such as Levi's, Chanel, Louis Vuitton, Harley-Davidson, Gunne Sax, Ralph Lauren, and designer labels often command the highest resale prices. Value also depends on rarity, condition, style, and era. Scroll up for a full list! Where is the best place to find vintage clothing? Many resellers source vintage clothing at thrift stores, estate sales, church rummage sales, flea markets, yard sales, storage auctions, and Facebook Marketplace. What are the best platforms to sell vintage clothing? Vintage performs especially well on Etsy, Depop, eBay, Poshmark, Vinted, Instagram, and Vestiaire Collective. Each platform attracts slightly different buyers, so crosslisting often leads to faster sales. How can you tell if an item is vintage? Look for details such as single-stitch construction, metal zippers, union labels, paper tags, natural fibers, and Made in USA or similar country-of-origin labels. Multiple indicators together provide stronger evidence of age. How should I handle vintage sizing in listings? Always include detailed measurements and explain the best modern fit. You can reference the tagged vintage size for accuracy, but sizing should be guided by measurements to reduce returns and confusion.

title: 5 steps to take control of your home purchase — even if the Fed won't lower rates
summary: The Fed isn't expected to cut rates July 28-29. Here's what buyers can actually control instead - from credit score to lender comparison.
body_text: Almost nobody expects a rate cut when the Federal Reserve meets later this month. Fannie Mae's July forecast has the 30-year fixed holding around 6.4% through the end of 2026. The Mortgage Bankers Association is even less optimistic, projecting 6.5% through 2026, 2027, and 2028. JPMorgan's chief U.S. economist says he doesn't expect the Fed to cut at all this year. You get the picture: If your homebuying plan depends on the market rescuing you with a lower rate, you could be waiting a long time. The good news? You could still buy an affordable home, despite the negative headlines that seem to be playing on repeat. The key is learning to control what you can control. Start with a pre-approval ...in as little as 3 minutes — no credit impact 5 ways to make homebuying more affordable No one can control or predict the global economy, but focusing on these five steps can help you buy an affordable home: 1. Work on your personal finances first Before you look at homes for sale, look at your own numbers. The stronger your personal finances, the less risk your file may represent to the lender. That's how borrowers with stronger credit profiles may qualify for lower interest rates, depending on the loan program and market conditions. Here's where to start: Pull your free reports from all three bureaus and dispute inaccurate data. Go to annualcreditreport.com to get started. Pay down revolving balances like credit cards. Doing this even before your next statement closes can lower your utilization ratio and your score within a single billing cycle. Pay off an installment loan, if possible. This will lower your debt-to-income ratio (DTI) which makes your loan application look better. Avoid big, unnecessary purchases which can deplete your savings or add to your monthly debt. If your credit score needs work, focus your energy where it counts. Knowing what debt to pay off first to raise your credit score can save you more in rate than waiting on a Fed decision ever will. 2. Know your price range by getting pre-approved A pre-approval isn't a formality. It's the tool that turns "maybe someday" into an actual number you can plan around. Pre-approval can show what a lender is willing to lend, based on your real income, assets, and credit, rather than a guess from an online calculator. Knowing where you stand saves time. It stops you from wasting time touring homes outside your real budget. It can also make you a more credible buyer the moment you find the right place. Even if you're not happy with the pre-approved loan amount, knowing where you stand can be a good starting point for improving your borrowing power (see step 1 above.) Start your pre-approval ...in as little as 3 minutes — no credit impact 3. Find houses you can afford Once you know your real borrowing power, use it. It's tempting to stretch toward a listing $50,000 above your pre-approval, assuming you'll "figure it out." That's how buyers end up house-poor: cash-strapped every month, with no cushion for a new roof, a job change, or a rate reset if they're in an ARM. Be sure to run your own numbers with a mortgage calculator before you fall in love with a listing. Factor in property taxes, homeowners insurance, which has climbed sharply in many states over the past few years. And keep your down payment estimate realistic. Some buyers can get approved with as little as 3% to 5% down. The more you can put down, the lower your monthly payment could go. 4. Compare lenders With average rates holding steady in the mid-6% to 7% range, many lenders are competing hard for every borrower. That competition can turn into leverage for buyers. Getting quotes from just two lenders can save the average borrower real money over the life of the loan; getting three or four quotes could increase those savings even more, according to research from Freddie Mac on rate dispersion in higher-rate environments. And the interest rate is only part of the picture. Two lenders quoting the same interest rate can have very different total costs (APRs) once you account for origination fees, underwriting fees, and credit report charges. These are all line items you can compare side by side on your Loan Estimates. 5. Find experts you can trust — and trust them A good loan officer and a good real estate agent do more than process paperwork. They tell you when a listing is overpriced, when a seller might negotiate, when a rate lock makes sense, and when it doesn't. Before you commit to working with anyone, ask direct questions: How many transactions have you closed in this price range this year? How do you communicate? What's your view on my specific market right now? Understanding what a real estate agent actually does day to day helps you evaluate whether the one you're talking to is doing that job well, or just showing up to open doors. The same standard applies to your loan officer. You're trusting this person with the single largest financial transaction most people ever make. Once you've vetted someone and decided they know what they're doing, let them do it. Constant second-guessing based on headlines rarely improves outcomes, and it can slow down a transaction at exactly the moments when speed matters most, like a home inspection contingency deadline or a rate lock expiration. The bottom line Waiting for the Fed to hand buyers a lower rate could mean waiting well past 2026, and even the Fed's own rate-setters aren't promising relief in 2027 either. None of that changes what's actually in your control: your credit, your debt, your search radius, your lender comparison, and the team you choose to work with. Buyers who spend their energy there tend to end up with a better-than-average rate, a better home, and a smoother closing than buyers who spend their time focusing on average rate charts. Frequently asked questions Will mortgage rates go down in 2026? Most major forecasters don't expect a significant drop this year. Fannie Mae's July forecast has the 30-year fixed averaging around 6.4% through the end of 2026, while the Mortgage Bankers Association projects roughly 6.5% through 2026, 2027, and 2028. JPMorgan's chief economist expects the Fed to hold rates steady all year, with the next move potentially a hike in 2027 rather than a cut. What's the first thing I should do before buying a house? Check your finances before you check listings. Pull your credit reports, address any errors, and look at your debt-to-income ratio. Strengthening these before you apply for pre-approval can meaningfully improve the rate and loan terms you're offered. How much do I need to improve my credit score to get a better rate? There's no single universal cutoff, but conventional loans generally reserve the best pricing for borrowers around a 740 score or higher. Even modest improvements, such as paying down a credit card balance or correcting a reporting error, can move you into a better pricing tier before you apply. What's the difference between pre-qualification and pre-approval? Pre-qualification is a quick, informal estimate based on information you self-report. Pre-approval involves the lender verifying your income, assets, and credit, and results in a letter that carries real weight with sellers and agents. If you're actively shopping for homes, pre-approval is the stronger tool. How many mortgage lenders should I get quotes from? Most experts recommend comparing at least three to four lenders. Getting multiple quotes lets you compare not just the interest rate, but the full Loan Estimate, including lender fees, which can vary a lot even when the rate looks similar. How do I know how much house I can actually afford? Start with your pre-approval amount, then subtract room for property taxes, homeowners insurance, and a realistic down payment — not just principal and interest. A mortgage calculator can help you model different price points before you start touring homes, so you're not emotionally attached to something outside your budget. Should I wait for rates to drop before buying a home? That depends on your personal timeline and finances more than on trying to time the market. Since most forecasts show rates holding in the mid-6% range through 2026 and into 2027, waiting indefinitely means potentially missing out on a home that fits your life today. Buyers who strengthen their own financial position tend to see more benefit than buyers who wait on the Fed. Get pre-approved ...in as little as 3 minutes — no credit impact Rates and forecasts referenced are national averages and third-party projections for informational purposes only and are not guaranteed. Individual loan terms vary by borrower qualifications, lender, and loan program.

title: ADHD Burnout in Adults: Causes, Symptoms, and Recovery Strategies
summary: For adults with ADHD, the ongoing stress of managing symptoms can lead to burnout, complete mental and physical exhaustion. This guide explains what ADHD burnout looks like, why it happens, and practical strategies to recover and prevent future episodes. Learn how to recognize the warning signs and build a toolkit of techniques that work with your brain, not against it.
body_text: Juggling life's responsibilities is tough, but for adults with ADHD, it can be even more overwhelming. Managing the symptoms of ADHD while balancing work, family, relationships, and self-care may feel like a constant uphill battle. Without proper support, treatment, and healthy coping mechanisms, the pressure can quickly build up. When this happens, the individual may experience immense exhaustion, hopelessness, and even feelings of depression. This is what's known as ADHD burnout. It's a common experience among many ADHDers, who often find themselves running on empty as they try to compensate for the unique challenges linked to this condition. What is ADHD Burnout? ADHD burnout refers to the mental, physical, and emotional exhaustion caused by the ongoing stress of managing ADHD symptoms. This often happens when you push yourself to your limit daily to keep up with your work and responsibilities. You're more likely to struggle with ADHD burnout if you're not receiving proper support or treatment for your ADHD. While not a medical diagnosis, it's a widely recognized experience among adults with ADHD who struggle with the constant effort of functioning in a world that isn't very ADHD-friendly. At its core, ADHD burnout stems from the constant effort required to compensate for executive functioning challenges [1] . This can include difficulties with: Time management : This is linked to time blindness and difficulty estimating how long tasks will take, making it harder to complete tasks on time and meet deadlines. Organization : A lack of organizational skills in ADHD might cause you to misplace essential items, documents, or information. Prioritization : Poor prioritization makes it challenging to distinguish between what's urgent and what's not. As a result, you may get quickly overwhelmed or focus on more interesting tasks rather than those that are complex or urgent. Impulse control : Impulsivity in ADHD may cause you to act upon distractions or temptations in the moment, which can derail your progress. Emotional regulation : ADHD can make it tricky to deal with difficult emotions like stress or anxiety [2] . Due to emotional dysregulation, challenges can quickly become overwhelming, leading to burnout. The mental energy required to navigate these challenges daily can be very exhausting. Many adults with ADHD feel like they're constantly playing catch-up with their tasks and responsibilities and are never quite able to get ahead or gain control over their daily lives. Over time, these struggles can erode their self-esteem and motivation, leading to frustration, exhaustion, and burnout. It's important to note that experiencing ADHD burnout doesn't mean you've failed or aren't trying hard enough. Being burnt out doesn't mean you're lazy, either. It's simply the natural outcome of trying to function at your best every day despite facing numerous challenges due to ADHD. The good news is that with the right support, strategies, and self-compassion, it's possible to break free from the cycle of burnout and regain your momentum forward. ADHD Burnout vs Regular Burnout ADHD burnout and regular burnout share some common features, including fatigue, reduced productivity, and feelings of overwhelm. However, regular burnout typically stems from external circumstances like workplace stress or prolonged caregiving, while ADHD burnout has distinct neurodivergent origins. Regular burnout generally develops in response to specific external pressures and may resolve when those stressors are removed or reduced. It tends to affect primarily one domain of life, such as work or a particular relationship, and recovery often follows a predictable pattern. In contrast, ADHD burnout arises from the constant internal effort of managing executive dysfunction, regulating attention and emotions, and navigating time blindness in everyday situations. It frequently impacts multiple life areas simultaneously and persists even when external conditions improve. Recovery from regular burnout typically involves rest, setting boundaries, and addressing the specific external causes. ADHD burnout, however, requires these steps, plus targeted strategies that accommodate executive functioning differences and neurodivergent needs. Common Causes of ADHD Burnout Common Causes of Burnout in Neurodivergent Individuals, Source: @neurodivergent_insights Executive Dysfunction Research has proven that ADHD can affect executive functions [3] . Executive functions are cognitive processes that support goal-directed behavior. Simply put, they affect your brain’s ability to regulate thoughts, emotions, and actions in order to achieve your desired goals. They are involved in your time management, self-organization, impulse control, self-motivation, initiation of tasks, and attention regulation. Adults with ADHD often experience executive dysfunction, making it harder to plan, prioritize, and stay focused. This constant mental effort can be draining and, over time, lead to burnout. When executive dysfunction makes everyday tasks feel like an uphill battle, it's easy to see how stress can build up. The ongoing pressure to meet expectations, whether at work, at home, or in relationships, can chip away at your confidence and motivation. As a result, you may constantly feel drained and overwhelmed. Masking ADHD Symptoms Because of the pressure to seem "normal" or fit in, people with ADHD often feel like they have to hide their symptoms. This is a coping mechanism known as "masking." ADHD masking refers to suppressing your symptoms and natural behaviors to live up to social and professional expectations [4] . In the long haul, this can be mentally and emotionally exhausting. Some common masking behaviors include: Mimicking the behaviors of people who do not have ADHD Over-organizing to compensate for difficulties with focus and memory Starting preparations for events or appointments far in advance and arriving much earlier than necessary Hiding stimming or fidgeting behaviors to appear calm Listening very closely and carefully during conversations to keep up Working twice as hard to meet deadlines or complete tasks that other people seem to find simple Masking behaviors in ADHD, Source: @truly_tish_adhd ‍ Over time, trying to "blend in" can take a serious toll, leading to exhaustion and burnout. This pressure to maintain a polished exterior can leave you frustrated and make you feel like you can never fully be yourself around others. Lack of Effective Coping Strategies Without effective ADHD-friendly coping strategies, stress can quickly build up and lead to an inability to start tasks, known as ADHD paralysis , as well as reduced productivity and burnout. Many individuals turn to unhelpful coping mechanisms that provide temporary relief but ultimately worsen things. Some common ineffective coping strategies include: Procrastination : Putting off tasks to avoid stress, only to face even more pressure later on Avoidance : Sweeping specific tasks or difficult situations under the carpet instead of trying to address them Overcommitting : Saying yes to too many responsibilities in an attempt to prove capability Perfectionism : Spending too much time on unimportant details, making activities take longer than they should Suppressing emotions : Bottling up frustration or stress instead of finding healthy ways to process them ADHD resources and communities can be incredibly valuable for finding practical coping strategies and learning how to thrive with ADHD. However, not everyone is aware of these resources or has easy access to them, so they may feel isolated or unsure of where to turn for support. Overcommitment and Perfectionism Many adults with ADHD have difficulty estimating how much time and effort tasks will take, often leading to chronic overcommitment. To compensate, some develop perfectionist tendencies, pushing themselves to meet unrealistic standards—only to end up overwhelmed and exhausted. The excitement of starting new projects or taking on new responsibilities can make it easy to overcommit. But when ADHD symptoms make it hard to follow through consistently, unmet expectations can lead to frustration, guilt, and eventually burnout. Signs and Symptoms of ADHD Burnout Signs and Symptoms of ADHD Burnout, Source: @fyidigital ‍ Mental and Emotional Signs of ADHD Burnout ADHD burnout takes a serious toll on mental and emotional well-being in different ways: [5] Chronic mental fatigue : Feeling mentally drained no matter how much you rest Loss of motivation : Struggling to start or complete tasks, even ones you used to enjoy Emotional detachment : Feeling disconnected from people, hobbies, or goals that once mattered Brain fog : Trouble concentrating, making decisions, or processing information clearly Heightened emotional sensitivity : Reacting more intensely to stress, frustration, or criticism Self-doubt and guilt : Blaming yourself for struggling rather than recognizing it as burnout These emotional struggles can trap you in a vicious cycle. Burnout symptoms may lead to greater self-criticism, which, in turn, intensifies the burnout experience. Physical Signs of ADHD Burnout ADHD burnout can lead to a range of distressing physical symptoms: Sleep disruption : Trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or feeling rested even after sleeping [6] Appetite changes : Skipping meals or overeating, leading to weight fluctuations Physical tension : Headaches and muscle aches from chronic stress [6] [7] Weakened immune system : Getting sick more often due to prolonged stress Low energy levels : Feeling physically drained and exhausted all the time Neglected self-care : Struggling with basic hygiene, nutrition, or other self-care habits Increased sensory sensitivity : Becoming more sensitive to sounds, lights, textures, or other stimuli These physical and mental symptoms don't exist in isolation—they feed into each other. This is why it's crucial to recognize the signs early so you can break the cycle and regain your balance. Impact on Daily Functioning ADHD burnout can disrupt nearly every aspect of daily functioning, making even routine tasks feel overwhelming. Burnout can affect your daily life in the following ways: Reduced productivity and performance at work or school Fewer social interactions due to exhaustion, which can lead to isolation Relationship conflicts or strain due to difficulty keeping up with commitments and maintaining healthy connections Disorganization or increased clutter in your home Financial hiccups resulting from job struggles or missed payments Addressing ADHD burnout is crucial because it can impact many different areas of life. Without intervention, these challenges can compound over time and make it harder for you to get back on track. ADHD Burnout vs Autistic Burnout ADHD burnout and autistic burnout share overlapping symptoms, including extreme fatigue, brain fog, and difficulties with executive functioning. Autistic burnout also comes with unique symptoms, such as increased stimming, meltdowns, shutdowns, heightened sensory sensitivities, and social withdrawal. While both forms of burnout have similarities, their underlying causes differ. ADHD burnout is driven mainly by the mental exhaustion of managing executive dysfunction, time blindness, impulsivity, and the relentless effort to meet expectations. In contrast, autistic burnout stems from sensory overload, social exhaustion, and the ongoing strain of masking autistic traits to fit societal norms. Both types of burnout require rest, self-compassion, and intentional adjustments to daily routines to support long-term well-being. The ADHD Burnout Cycle The ADHD Burnout Cycle, Source: @theliven.app ‍ ‍ ADHD burnout often follows a predictable pattern. Learning to recognize this pattern is important so it can be interrupted before it spirals out of control. It usually starts with enthusiasm. You may experience a surge of motivation and optimism about new projects or responsibilities. This excitement can often lead to overcommitment as you take on more tasks than you can actually handle. As your workload increases, the struggle phase begins. Executive dysfunction in ADHD can make it harder to stay consistent, meet deadlines, or complete tasks efficiently. As a result, you may compensate by working longer hours, skipping rest, or using unsustainable and unhealthy coping mechanisms to stay afloat. Eventually, these efforts become unsustainable, leading to overwhelm and exhaustion, and even the simplest responsibilities begin to feel impossible. Eventually, you may reach the breaking point, leading to burnout. This is when you experience energy crashes, low motivation, and hopelessness. Over time, there may be a recovery period where you might rebuild your energy and capacity. However, without meaningful intervention, this cycle can repeat and lead to burnout again. Strategies to Recover from ADHD Burnout Prioritize Rest and Self-Care Recovering from ADHD burnout starts with giving yourself permission to rest and care for your mind and body in a way that truly supports you. Here are some key ways to prioritize self-care: Improve sleep hygiene : Establish a consistent bedtime routine, limit screen time before bed, and create a cool, dark sleep environment to improve rest quality. Nourish your body : Eat balanced and nutritious meals to provide your brain the fuel it needs to function at its best. Move in ways that feel good : Whether it's stretching, walking, or dancing, physical activity can help release built-up stress and boost energy levels. Engage in restorative activities : Spend time in nature, explore creative hobbies, or try mindfulness practices that help you recharge. Embrace rest without guilt : Understand that taking breaks isn't lazy—it's necessary. You may also need to reduce your responsibilities temporarily as you recover. Remember that true rest isn't just about taking a break. It involves creating a lifestyle that prevents burnout from creeping back in. Set Realistic Expectations and Boundaries Having realistic expectations and setting clear boundaries can help reduce or prevent burnout. Here are some ways to do so: Instead of attempting a huge project head-on, deconstruct it into smaller and more achievable goals Learn to be okay with saying "no" if you're not able to cope with additional responsibilities or duties Be willing to seek or accept help from others when you know you've reached your limit Abandon perfectionism and start adopting a "good enough" mindset when appropriate Develop an ADHD-Friendly Toolkit Building a personalized ADHD toolkit can help you prevent or manage burnout more effectively. One powerful technique is the Pomodoro method, which alternates focused work sessions with short breaks to boost productivity. Visual reminders, timers, and productivity apps can also improve time management, focus, and organization, making daily tasks more manageable. Another helpful strategy is body doubling . This involves working alongside someone else to boost accountability and break through procrastination or ADHD paralysis. Apart from these strategies, you can also consider requesting ADHD workplace accommodations from your employer. These accommodations, such as a quiet workspace, noise-canceling headphones, or a flexible work schedule, may help you better manage tasks and responsibilities at work. For some, medication may play a key role in symptom management. If you're considering this option, consulting a healthcare provider can help determine whether it's the right fit for you. Additionally, seeking support from therapists, ADHD coaches, or support groups can also be a way to gain valuable guidance and advice for building sustainable coping strategies. Cultivate Self-Acceptance and Community Recovering from ADHD burnout also involves embracing self-acceptance and surrounding yourself with the right support system. Start by challenging negative self-perceptions and recognizing when you're being overly harsh on yourself. Instead of focusing on what you didn't do, celebrate small wins. Every achievement, no matter how big or small, is a step forward. Connecting with the ADHD community can be incredibly helpful. Support groups, online forums, and social media communities offer a space to share experiences and find support or encouragement from those who have been in your shoes. When to Seek Professional Help While self-help strategies are valuable, professional support may be necessary when: Burnout symptoms persist despite your best efforts You experience signs of depression or anxiety alongside burnout Functioning in daily life becomes close to impossible You're considering changes to medication or treatment plans It's always best to seek help from a trained medical professional, as they are in the best position to assess your symptoms and help you find practical solutions. The Path Forward ADHD burnout can feel overwhelming and isolating, but you're not alone. With the right strategies, support, and self-compassion, you can break free from the cycle and create a more sustainable, balanced approach to daily life. Setbacks are a natural part of the process, but the more you understand yourself and your ADHD, the better equipped you'll be to prevent and manage burnout. If you're looking for a supportive community to help you stay focused and productive, consider joining spaces designed specifically for adults with ADHD. Flow Club , for example, offers a structured environment where you can harness the power of body doubling to boost your motivation and accountability. FAQs What is ADHD burnout? ADHD burnout is a state of mental, emotional, and physical exhaustion that is typically caused by the stress and pressure of managing ADHD symptoms. It often results from pushing too hard to keep up with daily responsibilities while struggling with executive dysfunction, time blindness, and impulsivity. How can I recover from ADHD burnout? Recovering from ADHD burnout requires rest, self-compassion, and adjustments to daily routines. Prioritizing sleep, nutrition, and regular exercise can help improve your mood and restore energy levels. Additionally, you can experiment with ADHD-friendly strategies, such as the Pomodoro technique, body doubling, and visual reminders, to make tasks more manageable. You can also seek support from therapists, ADHD coaches, or support groups. What does ADHD burnout feel like? ADHD burnout can feel like a persistent mental fog, extreme fatigue, a lack of motivation, and a loss of enjoyment for the things you once looked forward to. Many people also experience heightened sensitivity to stress, feelings of guilt and failure, and lower productivity or performance at work or school. How long does ADHD burnout last? The duration of ADHD burnout varies from person to person. Some may recover in a few days or weeks with proper rest and support, while others may struggle for months if burnout is severe and left unaddressed. The key is to address burnout promptly rather than pushing through it. How can I get out of ADHD burnout? To break free from ADHD burnout, start by acknowledging that rest is necessary, not a luxury. Reduce unnecessary commitments and allow yourself guilt-free downtime. You can also explore ADHD-specific tools that make life easier. body_text: 7 tips for mobile banking safety Secure your finances with Dave's top 7 mobile banking safety tips. Stay safe while enjoying the convenience of mobile banking. Last updated: September 30, 2024 Mobile banking has revolutionized how we manage our finances, making it possible to make transactions from the convenience of smartphones. However, with convenience comes some increased potential risks. The consequences of a mobile banking security breach can be pretty severe. A compromised bank app could lead to a loss of funds, unauthorized access to sensitive personal data, and diminished trust in financial institutions. Users must protect their sensitive banking and financial data when using mobile banking apps to minimize the risk associated with using them. But how can people enjoy the benefits of online banking without putting their information at risk? In this article, we’ll provide seven mobile banking safety tips to ensure the security of your transactions and the safety of your personal information. Use official online banking apps from your bank Downloading the official mobile banking app from your bank or financial institution is vital. You can do this by visiting the Google Play Store (for Android users) or the Apple App Store (for iPhone users). Keep your eyes peeled for fake apps that pretend to be legitimate banking apps. One way to know if the app is legitimate is to check its reviews and ratings. Keep your mobile banking app updated App developers regularly release updates and patches to improve the performance and security of mobile banking apps. To keep your app running smoothly and minimize the risk of security threats, it's always a good idea to make sure you're using the latest version. Check for updates frequently and keep your mobile banking app up-to-date. Enable password protection and multi-factor authentication Password protection is a security measure that requires users to authenticate their identity by inputting a unique, confidential character string before being granted access. It is an essential layer of security for your mobile banking app. Use a strong password that's unique and complex enough that others can't easily guess it. It's also important to avoid using the same password across different accounts or services. Try not to use personal information like your birthday, address, or social security number. Bad actors can find this information online and use it to access your accounts. Another great security measure is multi-factor authentication (MFA). This means you'll have to provide identification to verify your identity. It might be a password, a physical token, or even your fingerprint. Most banks now offer MFA for added security. Be sure to activate these additional security measures to ensure that only you can access your mobile banking app. Never save login details on your device While saving your mobile banking password or login details on your device might be tempting for easy access, this practice can expose your financial data to theft or unauthorized access. Instead, use a secure password manager. This will ensure you have a convenient way to store, generate, and access your passwords without compromising their security. Practice safe Wi-Fi and data usage It's best to use your mobile banking app or conduct transactions when you're connected to private Wi-Fi networks, such as the one you have at home or your own mobile data plan. There are plenty of risks of accessing the app through public Wi-Fi networks because your data can be intercepted. Avoid using your banking apps in public spaces like airports and coffee shops, where anyone can access the Wi-Fi. Also, be cautious when using public USB chargers, as they can potentially be used to steal data from your device. When charging your phone in public places, it's better to use a portable charger or your charging cables connected to a power source to keep your data secure. Monitor account activity regularly One of the best ways to protect your mobile banking app is to stay informed about transactions within your account. Monitor your accounts frequently to ensure that you authorize all the transactions posted. This practice will help you identify any suspicious activity and promptly alert your bank to lessen the damage if any suspicious transactions arise. Protect your device from viruses and malware Last but not least, keep your devices safe from harmful malware attacks. Just like your computer, your mobile device can also be threatened by viruses, malware, and other security risks. To protect your device, make sure to install a trustworthy antivirus app and keep it updated regularly. Also, be careful when downloading and installing apps, especially from unknown or third-party sources. Some apps might contain harmful software that can steal your data or compromise the security of your device. body_text: Today we are announcing the release of our 2N intercom integration. This now lets you connect 2N intercoms and access systems to Seam and use our API + dashboard to control them. You can unlock doors, edit resident directory, and retrieve entry events. Most 2N intercom models come with a built in camera which we will release as part of our broader Universal Camera API later this summer. Resources: Check out our Getting Started with 2N Guide View the full list of supported 2N Devices What is 2N A subsidiary of Axis Communications, 2N manufactures and sells intercom and access control systems. The IP Verso and Solo models are arguably their most popular intercom products, which you’ll encounter at many buildings in San Francisco or New York. How Does it Work Seam’s 2N integration goes through the My2N cloud. You will need credentials to My2N as well as the on-prem unit you are trying to connect with. To start, create a new Connect Webview and select 2N as the provider. Then, enter your My2N cloud credentials. Seam will then retrieve all your devices. You will then be presented with a list of all these devices. Select the devices you want to connect. Seam will then present a login screen for each project as on-prem device will have its own login credentials. Once your devices are connected, you’ll be able to unlock the door, edit residents, retrieve events, and eventually tap into the camera feed of the device. Check out our Getting Started with 2N Guide for more info. What’s Next As mentioned, we’re going to expand this integration over time to include additional features like the ability to tap into the video feed. If you have any specific feature request or are running into issues, please contact us at support@getseam.com .
